html:
The Salinan are an Indigenous people of the Central Coast of California, in the southern Salinas Valley and the Santa Lucia Range. Their language was an isolate, not clearly related to any other. They gathered acorns, hunted and fished, and traded with neighbours such as the Chumash to the south, the Esselen and Rumsen to the north, and the Yokuts inland.

Spanish missionaries founded Mission San Antonio de Padua in their land in 1771 and Mission San Miguel Arcángel in 1797, part of the chain of Spanish missions in California, and most Salinans were drawn into them. Disease and mission life cut their numbers sharply, and after the missions were broken up in the 1830s their land passed to ranchers. Their descendants are seeking federal recognition.
